From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: merdé

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French merde (“shit”). Doublet of mierda and merd.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /mɛː(ɹ)d/
  • Rhymes: -ɛː(ɹ)d

Noun

[edit]

merde (uncountable)

  1. (mildly vulgar, chiefly humorous) Shit.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Meder, mered

Alemannic German

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian merda (“shit, crap”).

Interjection

[edit]

merde

  1. (Uri, vulgar) shit!, crap!

References

[edit]
  • Abegg, Emil, (1911) Die Mundart von Urseren (Beiträge zur Schweizerdeutschen Grammatik. IV.) [The Dialect of Urseren], Frauenfeld, Switzerland: Huber & Co., page 17.

Dutch

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French merde.

Interjection

[edit]

merde

  1. (chiefly Belgium, vulgar) shit!, crap!

French

[edit]
French Wikipedia has an article on:
merde
Wikipedia fr

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • m*rde (censored)
  • mrd (censored, Internet slang)
  • marde (Canada)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French merde, from Old French merde, from Latin merda.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /mɛʁd/
  • (Quebec) IPA(key): [maʁd]
  • Audio (France, Muntzenheim):(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France, Grenoble):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Agen)):(file)

Interjection

[edit]

merde

  1. (vulgar) shit!, crap!
    Merde ! J'ai oublié mes clés !
    Shit! I forgot my keys!
  2. (theater) break a leg!

Noun

[edit]

merde f (plural merdes)

  1. (vulgar) turd, piece of feces, shit
    J’ai marché dans une merde de chien.
    I stepped in dog shit.
  2. shit (something undesirable or unwanted)
    J'en ai marre de ce petit morveux de merde !
    I've had it with this little fucking brat!
  3. shit (something of poor quality)
    Aïe, cette télé de merde !
    Ugh, this piece-of-shit TV!
  4. (derogatory) a dickhead, a fuckhead, a bastard

Derived terms

[edit]
  • avoir de la merde dans les yeux
  • avoir un œil qui dit merde à l'autre
  • bonne merde

  • emmerder
  • être dans la merde jusqu'au cou

  • fouteur de merde
  • foutre la merde
  • je te dis merde
  • jeter comme une merde
  • merde alors
  • merdique
  • mouche à merde
  • ne pas se prendre pour de la merde
  • putain de bordel de merde
  • putain de merde
  • sac à merde

Related terms

[edit]
  • emmerder
  • merder
  • merdeux

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Dutch: merde
  • → English: merde

Middle French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French merde.

Noun

[edit]

merde f (plural merdes)

  1. (vulgar) shit (feces)
  2. (figuratively) shit (something undesirable)

Descendants

[edit]
  • French: merde
    • → Dutch: merde
    • → English: merde
  • → English: merd

Norwegian Nynorsk

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

merde f (definite singular merda, indefinite plural merder, definite plural merdene)

  1. alternative form of merd m

Old English

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmer.de/, [ˈmerˠ.de]

Verb

[edit]

merde (Anglian)

  1. inflection of merran:
    1. first/third-person singular preterite indicative
    2. singular preterite subjunctive

Old French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin merda.

Noun

[edit]

merde oblique singular, f (oblique plural merdes, nominative singular merde, nominative plural merdes)

  1. (vulgar) shit (feces)

Descendants

[edit]
  • Middle French: merde (see there for further descendants)
  • Walloon: miere
